newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen negative, buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen negative, buyers sidelined.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen languishing in negative territory on Thursday as investors took to the sidelines ahead of Friday's GDP figures, dealers said.
"It looks like we're marking time ahead of tomorrow's GDP numbers," a dealer with a local institution said.
Good figures could see the index burst through 2,100, otherwise it would remain rangebound at 2,050 to 2,150, he said.
At 0220 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index stood at 2,080.99, down 17.27, with losers leading gainers 129 to 20.
"We were expecting a bit of a rebound today, but it hasn't really happened," another dealer said.
Early volume was a low 46.2 million shares, with some 18.0 million of these traded in debut listing Poh Lian Holdings.
Poh Lian opened at a high of Singapore $0.58 against its S$0.42 offer price before settling back to S$0.515 at 0220 GMT.

Singapore Airlines foreign shares were also active on reports it was nearing a decision on taking a stake in Australian airline, Ansett. The counter saw 1.4 million units traded and stood down S$0.10 at S$13.10.
Early gains were led by Creative Technology, up S$0.90 at S$25.70. Losers were topped by OCBC foreign, down S$0.60 at S$18.30. -- Nick Edwards, Singapore newsroom (65 8703011)
